angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,305,133 km at 30.36 pc = 0.57 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69732: distance 30.358 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.005), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 30.358 +/- 0.152 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 32.5885 +/- 0.1410 mas (same row, RUWE 2.45), 231.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.876 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69732: radius 1.876 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 15.241 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.192) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,305,133 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8332 +/- 857 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69732: effective temperature 8332 +/- 857 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.061) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69732: effective temperature 8332 +/- 857 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.061) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.95 from 2021A&A...647A..49S; the 5 published values span log g 3.95 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A%26A...647A..49S)
